fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled IEC 60870-5-104 APDU length byte read from the TCP payload; this value drives all subsequent offset arithmetic in the parsing loop.
Control byte bit 0 selects the frame type; with bit0 == 0 the APDU is treated as Type I and enters the vulnerable ASDU parsing branch.
len is reduced by the 6 bytes of magic+len+4 control bytes and offset is advanced to the first ASDU byte; the reduced len is later used to advance offset past the APDU.

The only bounds check performed: it verifies that the declared ASDU fits in the payload, but it does not reserve room for the later 'offset += len + 2' advance and the subsequent 'asdu = *(u_int16_t *)&payload[4 + offset]' read, which lands 4 bytes beyond the advanced offset.

offset is advanced by the (reduced) ASDU length plus 2, landing one byte past the end of the APDU; when the APDU exactly fills the payload, offset == payload_len, so offset + 4 points 5 bytes past the payload.

Out-of-bounds read of 2 bytes: with a single I-format APDU (len byte L=72, payload_len=74) exactly filling the payload, offset == payload_len, so payload[4 + offset] reads bytes 78-79 of the payload, i.e. 5 bytes past the 74-byte TCP payload (4 bytes past the 128-byte packet heap buffer) -> ASAN heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2.

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: Heap buffer overflow (out-of-bounds heap read) in IEC104Stats::processPacket: the attacker-controlled APDU length byte makes offset advance past the end of the payload, and 'asdu = *((u_int16_t *)&payload[4 + offset])' reads 2 bytes 4 positions beyond the advanced offset without a sufficient bounds check.
